q-68372.name: Question 1
q-68372.worked_solution:
To raise a power to another power, we simply multiply the exponents:

$$
{({0.5}^{6})}^{3}={0.5}^{6\cdot 3}={0.5}^{18}
$$

q-68148.name: Question 5
q-68148.worked_solution:
To raise a power to another power, we simply multiply the exponents:

$$
{({(\frac{1}{6})}^{2})}^{-2}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{2\cdot (-2)}={(\frac{1}{6})}^{-4}
$$

To evaluate ${(\frac{1}{6})}^{-4},$ we find the reciprocal of the base $\frac{1}{6}$ and then raise that reciprocal to the same power but with the opposite sign:

$$
{(\frac{1}{6})}^{-4}={6}^{4}
$$

$$

$$
